newsitem.title: UK: Oftel raps BT for unfair launch of product.
newsitem.headline: Oftel raps BT for unfair launch of product.

text.p: UK telecommunications industry regulator Oftel said on Thursday that it believed British Telecommunications Plc (BT) had breached its licence in the recent launch of a new service without proper notification.

In a catalogue of criticisms of the so-called "ring back" service, Oftel said it was particularly concerned that the full impact of the service had not been brought to the notice of the British communications industry as a whole until after launch.
Thus, instead of being able to stop the launch as it would have wanted, Oftel has had to resort to seeking a number of pledges from BT to counter what it sees as outstanding problems.

In its statement Oftel said that, "in trials of the product, BT had ignored the interests of manufacturers and supliers of payphone equipment and not paid full regard to the interests of all consumers equally."

As well as unfairly favouring its own payphone equipment businesses over other competitors by failing to notify the industry in advance, "BT's manner of introducing the service also discriminated between classes of end customer".
Regulator Don Cruickshank said: "I am disappointed at BT's propensity to roll out services which run on the network with undue regard for the effect it might have on the suppliers and end customers".

BT has therefore been asked by Oftel to waive charges incurred as a result of unwanted items on customers bills caused by the new service, to make compensation payments for inconvenience and distress, to set in place "a comprehensive communications programme to raise awareness in the industry", and to brief its customer service staff to ensure queries are handled in a way that minimises any customer difficulties.
